1:concepts.text: Session identity. The session panel identifies the session and its configuration. It is metadata, not the answer and not proof that the current turn completed. Keep that identity while following the other panels. Streaming preview. The text preview helps you follow a response as it streams. A visible preview alone does not establish success. If the stream ends early, it may remain incomplete. Authoritative message. The authoritative agent message replaces its matching preview instead of being appended again. Compare the message identity and final text so the same answer is not displayed twice. Lifecycle evidence. Lifecycle events tell you when the session is running and when it becomes idle. Read the stop reason as well as the status. Idle with end turn supports normal completion; other reasons can mean a pause. Explicit outcome. Read the reported outcome independently from the answer text. A partial answer can coexist with an error or an incomplete stream. Requires action and budget reached are not normal successful completion. Execution boundary. An offline fixture teaches the event contract without calling a model. A live run is separate evidence and can incur charges. A local browser cancel does not by itself prove remote interruption or cleanup.

12:concepts.text: Retained session. This lesson retains one session while several messages are processed. Track its identity across turns. The host queue controls admission and ordering; this is not an Agent SDK asynchronous input generator. Local admission. When a message passes local validation, the host admits a command and assigns its own command identifier. Admission is not the same as provider acceptance and does not mean the turn has completed. Wait while busy. If the first message is still running, the next command stays in the host queue. It waits for completed idle evidence before submission. Follow the waiting count instead of assuming two simultaneous provider turns. Provider acceptance. A provider accepted user event has its own identity. Keep it distinct from the host command identifier. Correlate the accepted event, later messages and the outcome rather than treating all identifiers as interchangeable. Turn outcome. Inspect the reported result for each queued command. A completed first turn does not automatically certify a later turn. Verify both outcomes and confirm that the retained session identity is the one you expected. Explicit close. Closing the queue is an explicit operation. Waiting commands should be cancelled before submission, and cleanup evidence should describe what happened. Offline simulated cleanup and confirmed live archival are different evidence sources.
